issues.t: Automatic transmission harsh shifts, slipping or failure
issues.sym: Hard clunks on the 1-2 or 2-1 shift, a shudder going into overdrive, a flashing O/D light, slipping, or the van refusing to move. Owners report repeat failures at higher mileage.
issues.why: The 4R44E and 4R55E four-speed automatics (and the 5R55E five-speed added for 1997 with the 4.0L) wear their overdrive band, drum and seals, and the electronic pressure control solenoid and valve body can stick. Ford issued bulletins on wiring harness, torque converter and cooler contamination for these units.
issues.next: Have the codes read if the O/D light flashes and check the fluid level and smell. If it slips or won't engage, stop driving it hard. A rebuilt or used transmission is usually the sensible fix on a van this age, and the cooler lines should be flushed at the same time.

issues.t: All-wheel-drive transfer case can break and spray fluid (recall)
issues.sym: On AWD vans: a loud bang or vibration from under the van, fluid sprayed on the exhaust, a burning smell, or sudden loss of drive.
issues.why: Driveline vibration and a shifting bushing at the transfer case output shaft could crack the transmission or transfer case. Fluid could reach the hot exhaust and start a fire, or the driveshaft could separate. Ford recalled AWD Aerostars and installed a new bushing and an aluminum driveshaft.
issues.next: If you smell burning fluid or hear a bang from underneath, pull over safely and turn the engine off. Have a Ford dealer check that the recall was done on your VIN.

issues.t: Ignition switch can overheat and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: Smoke or a hot smell from the steering column, a hot key, dash gauges or fuses that quit, or the engine starting without the key fully inserted.
issues.why: Ford built these vans with more electrical load on the ignition switch's accessory circuit than the switch was designed for. The contacts can arc, short and overheat. Ford's fix was a jumper harness with a relay that takes the load off the switch.
issues.next: If you see smoke or smell burning near the column, turn the key off and get everyone out. Have a Ford dealer confirm the recall relay harness was installed.

issues.t: Accelerator cable can fray and stick (recall)
issues.sym: The engine is slow to drop back to idle when you lift off the gas, the pedal feels sticky, or the van keeps pulling after you release the pedal.
issues.why: Some 1997 vans with the 3.0L engine had the accelerator cable kinked during assembly, so the inner wires fray and drag. Owners also filed complaints about runaway speed and throttle cables coming loose from the pedal.
issues.next: If the throttle sticks, shift to neutral and brake hard, then turn the engine off once stopped. Have a Ford dealer check that the new cable from the recall was fitted.

issues.t: Aluminum wheels crack at the spokes
issues.sym: A wobble or vibration at speed, a clicking or roaring noise from a wheel, or visible cracks around the spokes or lug holes. Some owners found several cracked wheels.
issues.why: Dozens of owners reported the factory 14-inch alloy wheels cracking under the van's weight. Ford did not recall them, and some shops called it a design weakness.
issues.next: Look closely at each wheel, front and back, around the spokes and lug holes. Do not drive on a cracked wheel; replace it with a sound wheel of the right load rating.

issues.t: Front wheel bearing failure
issues.sym: Grinding or roaring from a front wheel that gets worse with speed, play in the wheel, or a pull to one side. In severe cases owners reported the spindle breaking and the wheel coming off.
issues.why: Worn front wheel bearings that are not serviced can overheat and seize, damaging the spindle, rotor and caliper.
issues.next: Have a grinding front wheel checked right away. A shop can check bearing play with the wheel off the ground; repacking or replacing the bearings early can prevent damage to the spindle.

issues.t: Rear axle bearing, seal or shaft failure
issues.sym: A growl or grinding from the rear, gear oil on the inside of a rear tire or brake drum, or, in rare cases, a broken axle shaft.
issues.why: Owners reported rear axle bearings and seals failing, sometimes blamed on rear brakes dragging and heating the axle end. One reported a broken rear axle shaft.
issues.next: Look for oil on the inside of the rear wheels. Have a noisy or leaking rear axle checked soon; a failed bearing can let the shaft move.

issues.t: Warped front rotors and pulsing brakes
issues.sym: The steering wheel or brake pedal shakes when stopping, the van jerks or pulls under braking, sometimes with pads that still look good.
issues.why: Owners filed many complaints of front rotors warping or cracking early. Ford issued several brake vibration and rotor machining bulletins for these vans.
issues.next: Have the rotors measured. Replacing them is often better than machining thin rotors, and avoid long downhill braking with a heavy load.

issues.t: Brakes fade or lose power after heavy use
issues.sym: A soft or low pedal, longer stops, or brakes that barely work after a long downhill run or heavy load.
issues.why: Owners reported brake loss, including one case where a mechanic found the calipers baked brittle by heat. The front brakes on these heavy vans work hard, and old fluid boils more easily.
issues.next: If the pedal goes soft, stop as soon as it is safe and have the brakes inspected before driving further. Flush old brake fluid and check calipers and hoses.

issues.t: Rear ABS warning light comes on
issues.sym: The ABS or brake warning light comes on, sometimes on and off, and the rear wheels may lock on hard stops.
issues.why: These vans use a rear-wheel anti-lock system. Ford issued a bulletin for the rear ABS light, and owners report intermittent ABS lights and rear lock-up.
issues.next: Check the brake fluid level first. Then have the ABS codes read; a sensor, wiring or the rear ABS valve is usually at fault. Normal braking without ABS still works.

issues.t: Rear brake drums stick or adjusters seize
issues.sym: Scraping from the rear, a drum that won't come off at a brake job, uneven braking or a weak parking brake.
issues.why: The rear drum brake self-adjusters wear and stick, which can leave the shoes dragging or out of adjustment.
issues.next: Have the rear brakes cleaned and adjusted at each brake service. Replace the adjuster hardware if it is seized.

issues.t: Oil leaks from the rear main seal and oil pan
issues.sym: Oil spots under the middle of the van, an oily underside, or burning oil smell after driving.
issues.why: RepairPal owners commonly report leaks at the rear crankshaft seal and oil pan gasket. Ford issued several bulletins on repairing oil pan gasket leaks that come back after a repair.
issues.next: Find the source before replacing parts and keep the oil topped up. A pan gasket is a moderate job; the rear main seal needs the transmission out, so it is often done during transmission work.

issues.t: Knocking noise from the 4.0L engine
issues.sym: A knock or tick that sounds like a bad rod bearing, often loudest on a cold start, then quieter as it warms up.
issues.why: Ford issued bulletins for 4.0L engine noise that can be mistaken for rod or piston knock, plus cold-start knock, and for oil priming after engine repairs. Low or old oil makes it worse.
issues.next: Check the oil level and have the oil pressure tested before assuming the worst. If the knock stays when warm or the oil light flickers, stop driving and get it diagnosed.

issues.t: Thumping coolant hose and swinging temperature gauge
issues.sym: A thumping or hammering sound from the engine bay and a temperature gauge that moves up and down.
issues.why: Ford issued bulletins for the 4.0L temperature gauge fluctuating with a thumping coolant hose. Consumer Guide notes the noise and erratic gauge come from a weak water pump; a revised pump was released.
issues.next: Watch the gauge; if it heads toward hot, pull over. Have the cooling system checked for trapped air and a weak water pump.

issues.t: Long crank or stalling after the van sits
issues.sym: The engine takes a long time to start after sitting for a while, or starts and then stalls, especially when coming to a stop.
issues.why: Ford issued a bulletin for a sticking idle air control valve on vans built through March 1996, and a computer reprogramming for stalling complaints.
issues.next: Have the idle air control valve cleaned or replaced and ask a Ford dealer whether the stalling reflash applies.

issues.t: Check engine light with misfire codes
issues.sym: Check engine light with codes P0300–P0306, sometimes with no running problem you can feel.
issues.why: Ford released computer reprogramming for misfire codes on the 4.0L. Worn plugs, plug wires or a coil can also cause real misfires.
issues.next: Have the codes read. If it runs smoothly, ask about the update. If it shakes or the light flashes, get it checked promptly to protect the catalytic converter.

issues.t: Heater core leaks
issues.sym: A sweet coolant smell inside, fog on the windshield, damp front carpet, or coolant level dropping.
issues.why: Ford issued a bulletin for heater core leaks on these vans. Old coolant speeds up corrosion inside the core.
issues.next: Check the coolant level and carpets. Heater core replacement is a large job; a shop may bypass the core temporarily so the engine doesn't lose coolant.

issues.t: Air switches to the defroster when accelerating
issues.sym: Airflow moves from the dash vents to the windshield when you climb a hill or accelerate.
issues.why: The vents are moved by engine vacuum. A leaking vacuum line or reservoir lets the doors fall back to defrost when vacuum drops, as described in a Ford bulletin.
issues.next: Have the vacuum lines to the heater controls checked for cracks. This is usually a simple fix.

issues.t: A/C compressor fails
issues.sym: A/C blows warm, the compressor makes noise, or the compressor clutch won't engage.
issues.why: Ford and Consumer Guide both note compressors on these vans fail when the system is low on refrigerant oil.
issues.next: Have the system leak-checked first. If the compressor is replaced, the system should be flushed and the correct oil amount added.

issues.t: Blower motor chirps or squeaks
issues.sym: A chirp or squeak from behind the dash on low fan speeds.
issues.why: Ford issued bulletins for blower motor squeaking at low speeds.
issues.next: This is mostly an annoyance. A new blower motor fixes it if it bothers you.

issues.t: Front axle oil leaks from the vent (AWD)
issues.sym: Gear oil on the front differential or underbody of an all-wheel-drive van.
issues.why: Ford issued bulletins for front drive axle fluid pushing out of the vent tube under some driving conditions.
issues.next: Have the front axle fluid level checked and the vent tube rerouted per the bulletin. Low fluid can damage the front differential.

issues.t: Power steering pump leaks or loses assist
issues.sym: Steering gets heavy, the pump whines, fluid leaks, or the pump pulley smokes.
issues.why: Owners report power steering pump leaks and loss of assist. Low fluid lets the pump overheat.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and look for the leak. Do not keep driving with the pump dry.

issues.t: Rapping or clanging noise when steering
issues.sym: A knock or clang from the steering when turning quickly or on rough roads.
issues.why: Ford issued a bulletin for rapping or clanging noise from the steering on these vans.
issues.next: Have the steering shaft and linkage checked for wear. Ask the shop about the Ford bulletin fix.

issues.t: Driver door latch may not hold (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign. The driver's door could open in a side impact if it was only partly latched.
issues.why: On some 1996 vans the driver door latch, when closed only to the first catch, did not meet the federal strength standard.
issues.next: Always close the door fully. Have a Ford dealer check that the latch inspection or replacement recall was done.

issues.t: Wrong rear tire pressure on door label (recall)
issues.sym: Rear tires wear faster than expected.
issues.why: The certification label listed the wrong rear tire inflation pressure. Ford mailed owners a corrected label.
issues.next: Use the corrected label or ask a Ford dealer for the right pressures, and check them monthly.

issues.t: Shifter won't come out of Park or interlock acts up
issues.sym: The shifter is stuck in Park, or it shifts out of Park without pressing the brake.
issues.why: Ford issued bulletins about the brake shift interlock being disabled by brake light faults. A burned-out brake bulb or switch problem affects the interlock.
issues.next: Check that the brake lights work. A brake switch or bulb is usually the fix.

issues.t: Sliding door won't latch or close properly
issues.sym: The sliding door takes several slams to close, won't latch, or rattles.
issues.why: Ford issued a bulletin for damaged or misadjusted sliding door latches, and owners reported latch failures.
issues.next: Have the latch and striker adjusted. A door that is not fully latched is a safety risk, especially with kids in back.

issues.t: Battery drains while parked
issues.sym: The battery is dead after the van sits for a day or two.
issues.why: Ford issued bulletins on dead batteries from an intermittent electrical draw.
issues.next: Have a shop measure the draw with everything off and pull fuses to find the circuit.

issues.t: Buzzing or rattling from the exhaust
issues.sym: A buzz or rattle from under the van at certain engine speeds.
issues.why: Ford issued bulletins for buzzing or rattling noises from the exhaust, usually a loose heat shield.
issues.next: Have the heat shields checked and clamped. It is not urgent unless a part is hanging.
